data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Extending an optimal 12-input network (39 comparators) via a parallel binary insertion of the 13th channel requires exactly 6 additional comparators (45 total) to satisfy the 0-1 principle; a budget of 5 additional comparators (44 total) will systematically fail verification.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the simulation discovers a 5-comparator extension that passes the 0-1 principle, the claim is falsified and S(13) <= 44.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 6-comparator extension fails the 0-1 principle for all tested base 12-input networks, the parallel insertion heuristic is structurally insufficient, not S(13) > 44.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"An optimal 12-input sorting network leaves 12 channels sorted. Inserting the 13th channel requires merging it into the sorted order. Using a binary insertion pattern, the 13th element can be merged in ceil(log2(13)) = 4 steps, but due to the constraints of the straight-line comparator network and the fixed wiring of the 12-input network, it takes 6 comparators. A sandboxed Python simulation can test this by taking a known 39-comparator 12-input network, adding a 13th channel, and randomly varying the placement of 5 vs 6 comparators to see if any 44-comparator network sorts all 8192 binary vectors.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
